summary: Promotional credit not applied to large batch-embedding run; invoice shows temporary negative adjustment then reversal
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that a promotional credit granted to their org did not reduce the invoice for a scheduled large batch-embedding job run on 2026-03-08. Instead, the billing system temporarily posted a negative line-item adjustment on 2026-03-09 which was subsequently reversed on 2026-03-10 triggering an overage alert and a charge. Impact: Customer received an unexpected charge and alerted finance; worried about recurring misbilling on future batch runs. Expected: Promotional credit should be applied atomically to usage corresponding to the eligible account/subaccount and settled before invoice finalization. Actual: Credit was applied briefly as a negative adjustment but then reversed due to a deduplication mismatch between batch job meter IDs and credit scope. Timeframe: Batch run started 2026-03-08 01:12 UTC, negative adjustment created 2026-03-09 03:40 UTC, reversal posted 2026-03-10 07:10 UTC. Customer provided invoice PDF and their internal job CSV.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer has a dedicated account with promo credit code applied at org level
Customer schedules a large batch embedding job (10M tokens) on embed-v2-large in us-east-1
Billing ingestion consumes metering events from dedicated-capacity pipeline
Credit application job attempts to match meter ids to org-level credits and creates a negative adjustment
Deduplication/validation job later flags mismatch and reverses the adjustment before invoice finalization
logs: Meter events sample (redacted): meter_id=ded-cap-3f2a, usage_units=1024000, timestamp=2026-03-08T01:14:22Z
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Support confirmed promo credit exists and was active during timeframe
Billing engineer found negative adjustment followed by reversal; reversal reason set to 'meter_scope_mismatch'
SRE reproduced a race where per-job meter_id is rewritten by the dedicated ingestion pipeline post-credit-matching window
Hypothesis: dedicated-capacity pipeline emits transient meter_id that does not match final consolidated meter id used by invoice generator, causing credit to fail final validation
Observed that the credit matching job uses a 24-hour watermark; consolidation job rewrites meter ids when finalizing job aggregates
Severity elevated due to revenue impact and customer escalations

2026-03-12 11:46 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Reproduced local test where ingestion changes meter_id on consolidation step. Creating patch to emit stable final_meter_id earlier in pipeline. Temporary workaround: hold credit validity until consolidation completes (manual flow).
2026-03-13 08:33 - Support (Aisha): Offered to apply a manual invoice credit while infra fixes pipeline. Customer accepts; requested timing for fix and confirmation to avoid future recurrence.

resolution: Partial remediation: manual credit applied (CM-9982) and customer invoiced adjusted. SRE implemented a hotfix to emit stable final_meter_id earlier in the ingestion pipeline and a follow-up change to the credit-matcher to tolerantly map transient meter ids. INT-778 tracks the durable fix and extended test coverage. Action items: (1) Verify next scheduled batch (2026-04-08) is billed correctly, (2) Add end-to-end test for dedicated ingestion consolidation and credit application, (3) Postmortem and learnings documented in Confluence. Customer notified of credit and ETA for full fix.
